question: The morphology goal asked for 229 pairs. Where does that number come from, and what is verifiable?

targetOrigin.reading: The target is the sum of region-survey footprint overlaps, the same construction behind the optical goal's ~727. It counts regions a survey's declared boundary contains, not candidates a survey can verify.

whatIsActuallyVerifiable.ceilingImposedByCandidateCount: A verdict is delivered on a candidate, and the register holds 34 of them. 195 of the 229 were unreachable before any survey was queried, because the candidates do not exist.

hst-jwst.note: 25 MAST observations overlapped candidate positions; loading the frames showed the nearest was 24.1 arcsec outside. One candidate was verifiable and no frame contained it.

euclid-q1.note: Containment tested against the real s_region polygon. Two candidates contained; one carries pixels and has a verdict, one returns an all-zero cutout.

outcome: The goal's stated outcome is that every surviving anomaly candidate in one of these footprints gets an independent-resolution verdict. Exactly one candidate has high-resolution pixels at its position across HST, JWST and Euclid Q1 combined, and it has a verdict: the eRASS1 X-ray source in dp2-tract-5063 has no optical counterpart at Euclid depth either. HST/JWST had marked that same candidate verifiable-but-not-covered, so Euclid closed the one case the first pass could not.
caveat: This says the goal's outcome is met for everything verifiable, not that 229 verdicts exist. They cannot: there are 34 candidates, and 33 of them have no high-resolution pixels at their position.
